notes:
SOURCE. English Wiktionary, read from the kaikki.org machine extraction (https://kaikki.org/dictionary/Chinese), extracted 2026-08-28 from the enwiktionary dump of 2026-08-05. Every row's sourceUrl is the Wiktionary page that renders the transcription; `sourceIpa` is Wiktionary's IPA string verbatim, so every conversion described below can be re-derived from the row itself. Nothing here was generated by a tool or a model - the repo's chinese-to-pinyin / to-jyutping / es-hangul packages were not used as a source for any field.

VARIETY. Standard (Beijing) Mandarin only: Wiktionary sounds tagged Mandarin + Standard-Chinese + Sinological-IPA. Rejected: Chengdu/Sichuanese, Xi'an, Nanjing and Dungan Mandarin, Taiwan-only variant readings, and every non-Mandarin topolect (Cantonese, Hakka, Min, Wu, Jin, Xiang, Gan) that shares the same headword.

SCRIPT. `text` is TRADITIONAL, because that is where en.wiktionary keeps the pronunciation section - Simplified pages such as 谢谢 are soft redirects with no IPA of their own. `simplified` carries Wiktionary's own Simplified-Chinese form where it differs (129 rows), so the same file serves the app's `zh` (Simplified) and `zh_traditional` codes.

ROMANIZATION. Hanyu Pinyin with tone diacritics, from Wiktionary's Standard-Chinese Pinyin line, in its CITATION form. `romanizationSandhi` is Wiktionary's own "phonetic" pinyin respelling where it supplies one (bù kèqi -> bú kèqi; yīqǐ -> yìqǐ): 13 rows.

TONE NOTATION. Wiktionary writes tone with Unicode SUPERSCRIPT digits, e.g. /ni²¹⁴⁻³⁵/. Each digit was rewritten to its Chao tone letter (1=˩ 2=˨ 3=˧ 4=˦ 5=˥). That is a notational re-encoding of the same Chao values, not a re-transcription. No ASCII digit survives in any `ipa`.

SANDHI. Wiktionary's superscript minus separates the underlying tone from its realisation: ²¹⁴⁻³⁵ means "214, realised as 35". `ipa` carries the SURFACE (realised) tone of every syllable - what is actually pronounced. `ipaCitation` carries the underlying tone of every syllable and is present only when the two differ. `sandhiTypes`: "t3" = the T3+T3 -> T2 rule; "yi-bu" = the 一 / 不 sandhi; "half" = allotony only (214 -> 21 half-third, 51 -> 53 half-fourth), which Standard Chinese applies to most non-final syllables and which pinyin never writes. 160 of 370 rows are marked `sandhi` (t3 43, yi-bu 61, half 139).

OPTIONAL ELEMENTS. Wiktionary's ²¹⁽⁴⁾ - a phrase-final third tone, optionally with the final rise - is rendered ˨˩, dropping the parenthesised element so no bracket survives in `ipa`. When scoring a phrase-final third tone, treat ˨˩ and ˨˩˦ as equivalent. `sourceIpa` preserves Wiktionary's original notation on every row, so the conversion can be re-derived or re-done differently.

NEUTRAL TONE is written by Wiktionary as a single digit whose value depends on the preceding tone (˩ after T4, ˧ after T2, ˦ after T3, ˨ after T1). It is a tone value, not a separate symbol, and it converts to a single Chao letter. In ISOLATION, though, a neutral-tone syllable has no contour to state at all and Wiktionary writes none: 了 le is /lə/, 得 de is /d̥ə/, 著 zhe is /ɖ͡ʐ̥ə/. Those rows carry `neutralToneOnly: true` and their `ipa` has no Chao letter - the one documented exception to "every Mandarin row is tone-marked". Toneless alternatives occur for the same reason and are not separately flagged. The particles are core vocabulary, so they are kept rather than filtered out to preserve the invariant.

SYMBOL INVENTORY vs Help:IPA/Mandarin (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Mandarin). Wiktionary is systematically narrower than the Wikipedia key; the differences are conventions, not errors. Diphthong offglides carry the non-syllabic diacritic (aɪ̯ ɑʊ̯ eɪ̯ oʊ̯ where the key writes aɪ aʊ eɪ oʊ). /a/ is written ä. Affricates carry tie bars (t͡ɕ ʈ͡ʂ t͡s where the key writes tɕ ʈʂ ts). Zero-initial syllables take a ˀ onset (二 = ˀɤɻ˥˩). Neutral-tone syllables take voiced-and-devoiced allophones (的 = d̥ə, 爸爸 = pä˥˩ b̥ä˩, 子 = d͡z̥ɹ̩). ɪ and ɔ appear as the allophones in -ɪn / -ʊŋ rimes. Syllabic ɻ̩ / ɹ̩ are used for the -i of zhi/chi/shi/ri and zi/ci/si, as the key prescribes.

VALIDATION. Every row's pinyin was checked programmatically against the IPA's underlying tone contour (T1=55, T2=35, T3=214, T4=51, neutral=single digit), syllable by syllable; where the two disagreed the row was dropped rather than guessed. The same check passes on 97.8% of the full 173k-entry Chinese index, so it is a real constraint rather than a rubber stamp - and its failures are Latin-letter headwords and kaikki parse artefacts, not bad transcriptions. Rows also pass: zero ASCII digits, no enclosing / or [ ], at least one vowel (or syllabic-consonant) nucleus, no leftover superscript, deduplicated on `text`.

SELECTION. Word tier: mine - HSK1-3-style core vocabulary plus deliberate diagnostics, including the 媽/麻/馬/罵 and 湯/糖/躺/燙 tone quartets that espeak-ng collapses to a single mˈɑ5-style form, retroflex vs alveolo-palatal pairs, neutral-tone compounds, and 一 / 不 sandhi. Sentence tier: 37 hand-picked common set phrases plus 63 harvested from Wiktionary's attested `phrase` and `proverb` headwords. Which items to include is my judgement; no transcription is.

MULTIPLE READINGS. 112 rows carry `ipaAlternatives`: the other attested readings of the same headword, with `romanizationAlternatives` and `sourceIpaAlternatives` positionally aligned to it - index 0 pairs with index 0 throughout. `ipa`, `romanization` and `sourceIpa` remain the PRIMARY reading (the one Wiktionary lists first), and the sandhi fields describe the primary only. An earlier version of this file kept only that first reading; across the curated candidate lists 120 headwords carried more than one attested reading and were silently truncated to one. None were ever REJECTED for having several, and none of the drops were mispairings - the agreement check between romanization and IPA found a consistent pairing for every reading it saw.

WHICH ALTERNATIVES ARE INCLUDED, AND WHY NOT ALL OF THEM. Wiktionary also lists readings no modern speaker uses - 不 fǒu / Fōu / fū / bū, 日 mì, 事 zì, 女 nǜ / rǔ - hanging off senses glossed "alternative form of ...", "original form of ...", "only used in ...", "a surname". A scorer that credits an engine with whichever reading it came closest to would hand out free marks for those, so a reading is kept only when its sound tags carry none of Erhua/dated/obsolete/archaic/nonstandard/rare, its entry has at least one sense NOT marked obsolete/archaic/historical, and the entry's gloss is a definition rather than a cross-reference. Changed-tone jyutping (jan4-2) collapses into its base reading (jan4). For 46 common heteronyms the readings are named explicitly instead of harvested, so the frequent cases are exact rather than exhaustive; every named reading was verified to exist on its page, and the one that did not (大 dài) was removed rather than invented. Elsewhere at most two alternatives are kept, in Wiktionary's own order, and only on the word tier. A stricter harness can ignore the `*Alternatives` fields and score the primary alone.

SENTENCE TIER, AND WHERE IT STOPS. Wiktionary does not transcribe running sentences - its usage examples carry pinyin but no IPA - so the sentence tier is whole-expression headwords: set phrases, four-character chengyu, and two-clause proverbs of up to 16 characters, a number of which are complete sentences (有志者事竟成; 種瓜得瓜，種豆得豆; 一分耕耘，一分收穫). The pool of attested, validating Mandarin phrase/proverb headwords is 8888, so 100 is a chosen cap and not a ceiling; raising it costs only compute. The fill favours rows exercising t3 and 一/不 sandhi, then spans the length range, so the tier runs from 3 to 16 characters. Two-syllable expressions were excluded from this tier on purpose - they are words, not connected speech.
